pharm: Reversibly inhibits the aromatase enzyme, blocking conversion of androgens to estrogens and lowering circulating estrogen in postmenopausal women.
quick: Cirrhosis/severe impairment: 2.5 mg every other day
No specific interaction; limit if dizzy
summary: Letrozole is a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor used in postmenopausal women for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer: adjuvant treatment of early breast cancer, extended adjuvant treatment after tamoxifen, and first- and second-line treatment of advanced disease. It markedly lowers estrogen levels. Common effects include hot flashes, arthralgia, and fatigue; long-term use reduces bone mineral density and can adversely affect lipids. It is contraindicated in pregnancy and lactation.
indications: Adjuvant treatment of postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer
Extended adjuvant treatment of postmenopausal women with early breast cancer who completed prior standard adjuvant tamoxifen
First-line treatment of postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive or unknown locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
Treatment of advanced breast cancer in postmenopausal women with disease progression after antiestrogen therapy

dosage.n: No dose adjustment for the indication

dosage.n: Median treatment duration ~5 years in trials

moa: Letrozole is a potent, selective, nonsteroidal competitive inhibitor of the aromatase (CYP19) enzyme. By blocking the conversion of androgens (androstenedione and testosterone) to estrogens (estrone and estradiol), it reduces circulating and intratumoral estrogen concentrations in postmenopausal women, depriving estrogen-dependent breast tumors of the hormone that drives their growth. It does not affect adrenal corticosteroid or aldosterone synthesis.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to letrozole or excipients
Women who are or may become pregnant; premenopausal endocrine status

preg: Letrozole is contraindicated in pregnancy and can cause fetal harm; it is indicated only in postmenopausal women. Verify postmenopausal status before use.
lact: Letrozole is contraindicated during breastfeeding; it is not known whether it is excreted in human milk, and there is potential for serious adverse reactions in the infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required for patients with creatinine clearance of at least 10 mL/min; letrozole has not been studied in severe renal impairment (CrCl <10 mL/min).
hepatic: No adjustment is needed in mild to moderate hepatic impairment. In patients with cirrhosis and severe hepatic impairment, exposure is increased; reduce the dose to 2.5 mg every other day.

major: Tamoxifen (concomitant use lowers letrozole plasma levels; avoid combination)
moderate: Other estrogen-containing therapies (counteract pharmacologic action; avoid)
minor: CYP2C19 substrates (letrozole is a weak inhibitor)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; moderate intake if dizziness or fatigue occurs.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise cholesterol/lipid levels on laboratory testing.

serious: Decreased bone mineral density / osteoporotic fractures

counsel: Take one tablet at the same time each day, with or without food
Hot flashes, joint or muscle aches, and tiredness are common
This medicine can weaken bones; your doctor may check bone density and advise calcium/vitamin D
Do not take if you could be pregnant; it can harm a developing baby
Report chest pain, leg swelling, shortness of breath, or sudden severe headache
pk: Estrogen suppression within days; clinical effect over weeks
Steady state in 2-6 weeks; sustained estrogen suppression
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C
pearls: Use only in postmenopausal women - confirm menopausal status before starting
Arthralgia is a frequent reason for discontinuation; manage proactively
Bone loss and fracture risk warrant baseline and follow-up DXA plus calcium/vitamin D
Avoid concomitant tamoxifen or any estrogen-containing product
Reduce to every-other-day dosing in severe hepatic impairment/cirrhosis
missed: If you miss a dose and it is close to the next scheduled dose, skip the missed one and continue normally. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Isolated overdose reports exist without specific symptomatic treatment guidance; there is no specific antidote. Treatment is supportive, including monitoring of vital signs and general supportive measures. Induced emesis may be considered if the patient is alert.
